title: MechSim scene v0.7b
description: v0.2 added surfaces, discs, loads (force and moment), fixed and roller supports; v0.3 adds rope, rod (Stab), pin and fixed joints, Festlager in free space and (v0.3c) the damper; v0.4 adds nodes (Knoten) and elastic bars for Fachwerke, bendable beams, cross sections (square, L, T, H, I; one Young's modulus for all) and harmonic loads; v0.4b lets elastic bars bend and buckle and adds viscous damping; v0.5 adds the optional end time t_max; v0.7b clamps Stab ends on blocks and discs (hinged_a / hinged_b). Version 0.1 to 0.3 scenes remain valid.

t_max.description: Optional end time of a run in s (the time bar of the UI). Ignored by the engine; without it the UI keeps its current setting (10 s at start).

view.description: Optional hint for the frontend camera. Ignored by the engine.

bend.description: v0.4: show the bending of beams this many times as large (display only; 1 = true to scale).

surfaces.description: Fixed line segments (v0.2). Pure geometry: supports sit on them, bodies do not collide with them. Ignored by the engine.

body.description: Body id, or null for ground.

point.description: Body-local point if body is set, world point if body is null.

p1.description: World start point. The hatching is drawn on the right-hand side of p1 -> p2.

dampingRate.description: Viscous damping rate alpha in 1/s (v0.4b): every node feels the force -alpha m v (and the torque -alpha J omega), so every mode decays like exp(-alpha t / 2) whatever its frequency; a load applied suddenly settles at its static response. It acts on rigid-body motion too (like a viscous medium), so leave it 0 for a body that flies free.

nodeParams.description: Knoten (v0.4): a point mass where Stabs meet. Stabs, supports and loads attach at its centre, [0, 0].

beamParams.description: Bendable beam (v0.4), lying along its local x axis. `position` is the point of the centroid axis at its middle. Anything may be attached to it at a body-local point (x within +-length/2).

mass.description: Total mass, kg. Default: density 7850 kg/m^3 times section area times length.

segments.description: Number of finite elements between the evenly spaced nodes (odd numbers are rounded up). Attachments get nodes of their own.

section.description: Cross section (v0.4), dimensions in m; one Young's modulus (210 GPa) for all. Bending is about the axis normal to the simulation plane. square: side a. L: leg height h, foot width b, thickness t. T: flange width b and thickness tf on a stem of width tw, total height h. I: two flanges (width b, thickness tf) at the top and bottom of a web (thickness tw), total height h. H: the I turned by 90 degrees (weak axis).

body.description: load: the body the load acts on.

rest_length.description: Relaxed length. If omitted, the initial distance between a and b is used. If it differs from the initial distance the spring starts loaded: tension (pulls the ends together) when the initial distance is larger, compression when it is smaller.

barParams.description: Elastic Stab (v0.4): a pin-ended member of steel with the given cross section, axial stiffness E A / L, unstressed as installed. Unlike the rigid rod (a constraint) it makes statically indeterminate trusses solvable. Since v0.4b it is also a beam-column: a chain of beam elements with hidden internal nodes, so it bends (under its own weight) and buckles (Euler load pi^2 E I / L^2, in the plane, about the axis of the section's I).

segments.description: Beam elements along the bar. 1 = the pure axial bar of v0.4: massless, no bending, never buckles.

mass.description: Total mass, kg. Default: density 7850 kg/m^3 times section area times length. The internal nodes carry it; half of the end segments hangs on the anchors as weight.

imperfection.description: Initial bow (a half sine, stress-free) as a fraction of the length: a seed for buckling (a perfectly straight column would only buckle when round-off grows). The default 1e-5 does not disturb the statics of a truss; 1e-3 is a typical real imperfection and magnifies the deflection of a column below its Euler load by 1 / (1 - P / Pcr). 0 = straight.

c.description: Damping coefficient in N s / m: the force is c times the rate of change of the length between the ends (tension while they move apart). At least one end on a mass, the ends on different masses.

force.description: World-frame vector, N (constant) or N s (impulse). Does not rotate with the body.

moment.description: Couple, N m (constant) or N m s (impulse), counter-clockwise positive.

mode.description: constant acts for the whole simulation; impulse is a velocity jump at t = 0 (and after every reset); harmonic is force and moment times sin(2 pi f t + phase), the excitation of a forced vibration.

frequency.description: harmonic only (required there): exciting frequency f in Hz (angular frequency Omega = 2 pi f).

phase.description: harmonic only: phase angle in rad.

body.description: Supports: the mass the support is on. pin_support only: null = Festlager in free space (point is then a world point).

point.description: Supports: body-local point (world point for a free-space pin_support). The support is fixed at its initial world position.

surface.description: Supports: optional id of the surface the support sits on (editor reference only; the engine uses params.angle).

a.description: rope, rod: first end. pin_joint, fixed_joint: point on the first mass.

b.description: rope, rod: second end. pin_joint, fixed_joint: point on the second mass.

endCondition.description: v0.7b. A Stab end on a block or a disc is clamped there (an Einspannung: the Stab keeps its angle to the mass, so the Stab is a rigid arm of the mass); true makes the end a pin (Gelenk) instead. Ends on nodes, beams and the ground are always pins (a node with an Einspannung clamps an elastic Stab).

length.description: Maximum length. If omitted, the initial distance between the ends is used (taut). Must not be shorter than the initial distance; longer means the rope starts slack.

angle.description: Direction of the supporting surface line in rad, counter-clockwise from +x, chosen so that the body lies on its left side (angle 0: floor below the body). roller_support slides along this line and reacts normal to it; the other supports use it for the symbol only.
